beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Fri Oct 16): conditional for beginners. Best 6:45–9:45 AM around the 8:13 AM high (1.8 ft), before the trades and gusts build. Long-period (16–18 s) south swell holding near or above average; Canoes 1–2 ft this evening. Afternoon not recommended. beginner.recommendation: Plan for early: 6:45–9:45 AM gives the most water over the reef (8:13 AM high, 1.8 ft) and the lightest wind of the day. Friday trades are forecast stronger than Thursday (NWS E 15–20 mph, gusts increasing; models 18–20 mph gusting 25–29 mph by mid-morning), cross-offshore at Waikīkī, so expect seaward drift that grows through the morning. The south swell is 16–18 s: Canoes read 1–2 ft this evening, but long lulls and occasional stronger sets are likely, so don't treat it as low-energy. Watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes) before starting. The DOH list was not read: check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side; brown, gray or cloudy water ends it. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if drift is low and sets aren't reaching the inside. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.headline: DOH advisory list not read this run; water quality at Canoes not verified
water.statement: No DOH water-quality list (brown water, bacteria, sewage) could be read this evening, so nothing can be said with certainty about Waikīkī, Oʻahu or statewide notices for Friday. A bacteria advisory at Waimea Bay (Oʻahu North Shore) was reported Oct 15 by a third-party repost and is not verified from DOH; it is not a Waikīkī notice. Not finding an advisory does not prove the water is clean. Check water color.
water.why: The eha-cloud live list could not be fetched (seventh run in a row); the Waikīkī Aquarium page and a third-party beach-water site did not render a live list (that site's ratings are estimates, not advisories). News: Waimea Bay bacteria advisory (Oct 15, Howzit Kohala); Kauaʻi brown-water advisories at Kōloa Landing (Oct 14) and ʻAnini Beach (Oct 13). Mostly dry leeward weather Friday morning lowers runoff risk at Waikīkī but proves nothing; showers increase Friday afternoon and night.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; stay out of affected water for 48–72 hours after rain stops.
